newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN CERA BANK LOOKING AT POTENTIAL PARTNERS.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN CERA BANK LOOKING AT POTENTIAL PARTNERS.

text.p: Cera Bank, Belgium's sixth-largest bank, said it is looking at potential partners, but denied that it was it talks with Banque Indosuez Belgique.
Financial daily newspaper L'Echo said on Wednesday that Cera was studying the possibility of buying Indosuez Belgium.

"We are always interested in potential partners and we are looking at a number of them at the moment. The future evolution (of financial markets) will force us to make alliances," Cera spokesman Stef Leunens told Reuters.
He added that Cera was not in talks with any particular bank at this moment.
Indosuez Belgium management committee member Etienne Brusselmans declined to confirm or deny L'Echo's report.
"We are thinking of several possible development projects for the bank. There are a number of scenarios. We want to continue the bank's development," Brusselmans said.
Indosuez Belgium is nearly 100-percent owned by its French parent Banque Indosuez . It is strongly focussed on financial markets and has a large trading room in Brussels.
French Compagnie de Suez sold 51 percent of Banque Indosuez to French bank Credit Agricole and is set to sell it a further 29 percent in July 1997.
Like Credit Agricole, Cera is a bank which focusses on the agricultural sector but Brusselmans said this should not lead to the conclusion that Indosuez Belgium would be sold to Cera.
"One should not jump to conclusions to quickly," he said.
At the end of June 1996, Cera had assets worth 1,241 billion francs and earned a 2.9 billion franc consolidated net profit.
Indosuez Belgium had assets worth 225 billion francs at the end of 1995 and earned a 418 million franc net profit.
